## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Diṭṭhikathā* ("Discussion of Views") is the second treatise (Ps 1.2) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, located in the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Frauwallner 1995; SuttaCentral; Wayman 1984]. Exemplifying the work's systematic and analytical method, the text opens with a catechismal interrogation: *kā diṭṭhi? kati diṭṭhiṭṭhānāni? kati diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhānāni? kati diṭṭhiyo? kati diṭṭhābhinivesā? katamo diṭṭhiṭṭhānasamugghāto?* ("What is view? How many bases of views are there? How many obsessions of views? How many views? How many dogmatic adherences to views? What is the eradication of the basis of views?") [Frauwallner 1995]. It defines *diṭṭhi* as *abhinivesa-parāmāsa* ("holding on to conviction") and proceeds to illustrate how entities become objects of grasping, utilizing an extended list of nineteen faculties (*indriya*) alongside the aggregates (*khandha*), sense bases, and elements [Gethin 2001].

Doctrinally, the text classifies views into twenty modes of individuality or reifying view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), applied in four ways across each of the five aggregates and designated as "aspects" (*ākāra*) [Wayman 1984]. The *Diṭṭhikathā* categorizes these into annihilationist views (*uccheda-diṭṭhi*)—such as observing any of the five aggregates as self—and eternalist views (*sassata-diṭṭhi*), such as observing the self as having form, form as being in self, or self as being in form [Wayman 1984].

SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus both highlight the treatise's extensive intertextuality with core Nikāya and Abhidhamma formulations [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral notes connections to suttas examining views and aggregates, including the *Cūḷavedalla Sutta* (MN 44), *Mahāpuṇṇama Sutta* (MN 109), *Paṭipadāsutta* (SN 22.44), *Dutiyaisidattasutta* (SN 41.3), and Abhidhamma expositions in the *Khuddakavatthuvibhaṅga* (Vb 17) and *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.3.1) [SuttaCentral]. In agreement, DharmaNexus records 6,951 Pali-internal reuse passages across 189 texts, with primary overlaps occurring in the *Khandha Saṁyutta* (SN 22), the *Abyākata Saṁyutta* (SN 44), MN 109, MN 44, Vb 17, and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus indicate textual reuses and parallels in Chinese texts (e.g., T 24 and T 125), Sanskrit treatises including Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* and Vasubandhu's *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, and Tibetan canonical translations including the *Mahāvyutpatti* (D 4346) and the *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
